questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
NTNUI is a sports club organising all sort of sports. Use the cabins available through NTNUI
Studentersamfundet is also a perfect place for a beer, party, debat or movie

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Cabin trips, hikes in Bymarka, cross country skiing

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The outdoor life and easy acces to the equipments (through Bumerang), which you would use for the outdoor activities

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Use the cabins through NTNUI
Register to more courses than you need and decide later
Go to Studentersamfundet

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Consider living in a private housing. Most people I spoke to prefers this.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I really liked the lifestyle of going to the mountains in weekends and skiing before/after class. The outdoor life was super appreciated.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To keep in mind that I didn't need to study hard and get good grades. To enjoy all the experiences outside studying more.
